docs.title: Core Rules
docs.html:
Umbra Caelis TTRPG is a story-driven system built on the d20. The GM may use other dice to color actions, but the backbone of the system is the d20. The system shares its core with SHZ-TTRPG; perks, stat progression and leveling up are exactly the same. The ability and class system, however, is unique to Umbra Caelis.

ROLLS AND DIFFICULTY

Formula: d20 + stat + bonuses. The GM judges the result against the difficulty of the task.

The GM sets the difficulty. There is no fixed difficulty table or target number. The GM weighs the difficulty of each roll according to the scene, the opponent and the circumstances, and does not have to tell the player.

The words Easy, Medium, Hard, Very Hard and Uber in ability and perk texts are not numbers but a description of difficulty given to the GM: "Medium" means an average task in that scene, "Hard" means one noticeably tougher. In the texts the difficulty is written in parentheses next to the roll: "d20 + Sebahat (Medium)".

Step: The phrase "the roll gets one step easier/harder" means +3 or −3 to the roll. A wound "advancing 1 stage" is separate from this; that is the wound stage on the Body and Wounds page.

Strong success: On a successful roll, if the d20 itself shows 15 or higher, it is a strong success. Some abilities grant an extra effect on a strong success.

Bonus cap: The total of bonuses to a roll coming from sources other than the stat (abilities, perks, conditions, Corruption, easing) is added to the roll only up to the bonus cap. The cap is +4 at the start of the game and rises by 1 each time the character reaches a new tier: +4 at Lv 0, +5 at Lv 5 (T2), +6 at Lv 10 (T3), +7 at Lv 15 (Peak). It can be at most +7; each step that makes the roll easier counts as +3. Penalties have no cap.

Overflow bonus: Bonuses above the cap are not lost; they become part of how the action is narrated. The GM turns them into outcomes outside the roll: the action's penalty or cost not applying, the task finishing faster, quieter or cleaner, a small extra benefit, and so on. For example, a character with a cap of +5 (Lv 5–9) and a total bonus of +7 adds +5 to the roll; in exchange for the remaining +2, the GM may waive a penalty the action would normally bring. The GM decides what the overflow bonus earns.

Nat20 and Nat1 are judged regardless of difficulty. They represent the best/worst possible outcome.

STATS

The list of stats and their meanings is in the Stats file. Stats have a minimum of 0 and a maximum of 10.

Which stat is used in combat:

  • Melee: Heavy weapons and grappling use Yalman; light weapons and swordplay use Kaçınç.
  • Ranged attack: Görü.
  • Dodging and parrying: Kaçınç.
  • Magic: Efsun (in some branches the ability file specifies another stat).
  • Mental resistance (fear, Cower, mind control): Sebahat.
  • Mental pressure (intimidation, commands, interrogation): Hakimiyet.

When in doubt, the GM has the final say.

SPELL ROLL AND DECAYED ROLL

  • Spell roll: Any action roll made with mana (usually Efsun). The types of mana and how magic works are on the Mana page. On a Nat1 on a spell roll, the mana backlashes: the character rolls d20 + Sebahat (the GM sets the difficulty, usually Easy); on a failure they gain +1 Corruption.
  • Decayed roll: Rolls made with Decayed Mana, dead souls, esoteric religions and dream powers. The ability file carries the note "This ability's rolls are decayed rolls". The decayed roll effects in the Corruption table apply to these rolls.

ABILITIES AND IMPROVISATION

An ability is not permission, it is assurance. Anyone can attempt anything with a stat roll. An ability is not a requirement for doing the task; it makes it more reliable, more powerful or less costly. Someone without Bonebreaker can still try to break a bone; there is just no guarantee. The GM does not ask the player "which ability are you using?" but "what are you doing?".

Improvisation: A player may want to use an ability in a way not written on the sheet (deflecting an arrow with Parry, carving Ward Rune into a door, and so on). If the GM finds it reasonable, the player accepts a harder roll: the roll gets one step harder and is made with the ability's normal stat. On a success, the ability's effect happens in the way the GM adapts it to the situation. Improvisation has no usage limit and no Inspiration cost; if the ability has its own cost (Corruption, Flow, losing a turn, etc.), that is paid.

Rollless effects: Effects that hit or count as successful without a roll exist only in the Vertex abilities of T3 branches. Other abilities roll, make the roll easier or worsen the wound.

Lockdown: With effects that leave a target unable to move, attack or cast spells, the target makes an escape roll at the end of each turn unless the ability says otherwise.

CONDITIONS

  • Cower: The character freezes in fear. Until the condition passes they cannot take actions; at the start of each turn they roll d20 + Sebahat (Medium) to break free. Cower is triggered by abilities, perks and moments of terror.
  • Fracture: A broken limb. It imposes a penalty on rolls using that limb in addition to the wound penalty. A bandage does not fix a Fracture; it only heals with a splint and a long rest, or with healing (see Bonebreaker).

DEATH

Death happens when the character dies as a result of RP. The state of the limbs (Body and Wounds) and the rolls made in the last action may, at the GM's discretion, result in the character's death.

DEATH SAVE THROW

When the character faces death, it is used as a last resort if they have the right to it. GMs are advised to turn this system off for tables seeking a challenge.

Every character has 1 Death Save. It is renewed by spending Inspiration Points (the Inspiration Points needed increase by 1 with each renewal).

The player rolls a d6. On 1-2-3, a mark goes in the Death box; on 4-5-6, a mark goes in the Save box. Whichever reaches 3 first happens. Death: the character dies. Save: the character survives, critically wounded.

INSPIRATION POINTS

Given by the GM in return for good RP or as compensation for a GM mistake. Solving a scene creatively without using abilities, by using something in the scene or the character's past, also earns Inspiration. 1 Inspiration lets you reroll a die. More than one Inspiration may be spent for decisions that could count as meta. If Inspiration drops below zero (a penalty or a debt agreed with the GM), the player takes -2 per negative point on every roll they make.

CLASS SYSTEM

At the start of the game the player chooses one of 4 main classes. The main class does not change for the rest of the game.

  • Close-Quarter: Masters of melee.
  • Hunter: Trackers, ambushers, hunters.
  • Priest: Bearers of faith and will.
  • Scholar: Theorists of mana and sorcerers.

Each main class consists of 3 tiers. Each tier has 2 branches, and in each tier the player chooses only one of them. The branch chosen in one tier does not restrict which branch is chosen in the next tier (e.g. Close-Quarter: Brute → Arcanist → Shinigami).

TierUnlocksLevels that grant points
Tier 1 (T1)Level 0Lv 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 → 5 points
Tier 2 (T2)Level 5Lv 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 → 5 points
Tier 3 (T3)Level 10Lv 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 → 5 points
PeakLevel 151 free point

Tier lock: Ability points earned after a tier unlocks can be spent only in that tier. A point earned in T2 cannot be spent in T1 or T3. Unspent points wait in the tier.

Peak point: A character who reaches Level 15 gets 1 free point to spend in any tier.

BRANCHES AND ABILITIES

Each branch has 5 abilities. There are no prerequisites within a branch; abilities unlock freely. Stat requirements provide the order. Since a tier gives only 5 points, a player can never fill an entire branch; they decide for themselves what to sacrifice.

  • Unlocking an ability: 1 point (the ability unlocks at level 1).
  • Raising a level: 1 point per level.
  • Level 3 lock: An ability's 3rd level can be taken at least 2 levels after the tier unlocks (T1: Lv 2, T2: Lv 7, T3: Lv 12).
  • Vertex abilities: Each branch has two Vertex abilities: the peak of the branch, single-level and with heavy requirements. Their names are usually Latin, German or Spanish.

Stat requirements are built on the branch's symbol stat:

TierEntryMediumHeavy
T1None / 12–34
T22–345–6
T33–45–67

Synergy: Some abilities gain an extra effect when taken together with a specific ability from another branch. These effects are written in the ability files under the SYNERGY heading. Synergies are mostly between different tiers of the same main class, so every path produces a different character.

ABILITY FILE

CLASS:        Main class
BRANCH:       Name of the branch (its tier)
TYPE:         Active / Passive / Reaction
REQUIREMENT:  Stat requirements (Lv: character level)
LEVELS:       1 / 2 / 3 or 1 / 2 or 1
  • Active: Used by spending a turn.
  • Passive: Always in effect.
  • Reaction: Triggers when an event happens, without spending a turn.

LEVELING UP AND STAT PROGRESSION

Leveling up is traditionally done at 1/2 level per session; the final decision is the GM's. The game has no built-in EXP system. The level cap is 15.

STARTING OUT

  • The player starts at Level 0, with 1 ability point and the branch chosen in T1.
  • 2 + 2 stats: 2 points go to the symbol stat of the T1 branch. The other 2 points are distributed among any stats except the symbol stat.
  • The starting bonus of the chosen T1 branch is applied (written in the branch's a.DAL file).
  • Perks are chosen (Character).

EVERY LEVEL (2 + 1 STATS)

  1. Action stat: +1 to a stat chosen by the GM based on the character's actions during that level.
  2. Symbol stat: +1 to the symbol stat of the branch in the tier where the point was earned. (Lv 1-4: T1 branch, Lv 5-9: T2 branch, Lv 10-15: T3 branch. At Lv 5 and Lv 10, when the tier unlocks, the new branch is chosen before this point.)
  3. MVP stat: An extra +1 stat to the MVP chosen among all players who level up.

If the symbol stat has reached 10, that level's guaranteed point goes to another stat of the player's choice.

Since not every player has to level up at the same time during a session, MVP points may be handed out late. To keep this point from being delayed too long, a player who is 3 or more levels behind the level the MVP is awarded for is not counted in the MVP pick. Example: (A: Lv3, B: Lv6, C: Lv7 → the Lv6 MVP is decided between B and C.)

docs.title: Character
docs.html:
COSMETICS

1- Character Name

The name the character will use throughout the story. It does not directly affect RP, but choosing a name that fits the character's house and region is recommended (Leit'ateirr nobles, Xitochi clans and the peoples of the Realm of Sand carry different naming traditions).

2- Character Age

Character age must be between 18 and 60. Exceptions may be made for over 60. For elves and dwarves, age is set with the GM.

3- Race

Human, Elf (Silverarrow), Dwarf (Ironsmith) or another race approved by the GM. Race has no mechanical effect; it only shapes RP and how the world treats the character.

4- House and Title

The house, army unit or institution the character belongs to (a Velites knight sworn to Sanders, a Savarum sorcerer of Blaze, a priest in the Trifarium church, and so on). The house card is placed on the sheet.

5- Faith

The religion the character believes in. It is mandatory for the Priest class and has a mechanical effect (see Priest). For other classes it is RP information.

6- Lumre

The game's currency. Putting it at the center of the story is not recommended, but it is used in trade, bribery and gambling.

7- Food

The provisions the character carries. On long journeys the GM may track them.

8- Corruption

The soul's level of corruption, 0-15. Abbreviated as Decay on the sheet. See Corruption.

9- Body Table

The health, bandage and armor state of the limbs. See Body and Wounds.

10- Inspiration Points

See Core Rules.

ATTRIBUTES

Every character has 3 separate attributes:

STATS

The statistic points used in in-game rolls and needed to unlock abilities. Stat points are affected by perks and leveling up. See Stats, Core Rules.

PERKS

Perks are chosen at the start of the game and affect the character's RP throughout. Positive perks cost perk points, negative perks grant perk points. The player starts with a starting amount set by the GM and may take as many perks as they like as long as the total does not drop below zero. Perks marked "Mutually Exclusive" cannot be on the same character.

Points left over after choosing perks are converted into stats:

(Perk Points to Convert + 1) / 2 → Round Down

The recommended starting amount for GMs is +0 or +2. Giving more makes the game easier.

Negative perk cap: At most +10 perk points in total can be gained from negative perks. More requires GM approval.

A weakness you never face is no weakness: The GM may reject, or lower the points of, a weakness the character will never encounter during the game (such as someone who doesn't use magic taking Volatile Mana). Every negative perk should really be felt at the table.

PERK POINT SCALE

PointsWhat it means
1-2Perks that add color or are useful in a narrow area
3-4Perks that are regularly useful; +2 stats falls in this range
5-6Perks that noticeably change how the character plays
8-9Rarely taken perks that define the character

Leftover perk points convert to stats as (points + 1) / 2; so 3 points is worth about 2 stats. A perk should be more interesting than the stats its points would buy.

PERK CATEGORIES

Perks are divided into seven categories: Origin (where you come from), Bond (who and what you are tied to), Body, Mind, Skill, Mana and Addiction.

A suggestion for players building a character for the first time: pick one Origin, one Bond and one weakness. The Origin gives the character a past, the Bond gives the GM a story hook, and the weakness gives a moment to play out at the table. Examples:

  • Old Soldier + Sworn Sword + War-Shaken: a knight back from the war, still bound to their lord but unable to bear the sound of gunpowder.
  • Street-Born + Old Friend + Branded: a fugitive who escaped the galleys and has a single friend in a port city.
  • Academy Graduate + Rival + Honest to a Fault: a sorcerer who outshone everyone at the academy but couldn't hold on at court because they cannot lie.
  • Hidden Heir + Dependent + Superstitious: a peasant who doesn't know their roots, looks after a younger sibling and sees a prophecy in every sign.

ABILITIES

Active, passive and reaction abilities unlocked through the main class and branches. See Core Rules, Class System.

CHARACTER CREATION ORDER

  1. Cosmetic details (name, age, race, house, faith).
  2. Choose the main class.
  3. Choose the T1 branch and apply its starting bonus.
  4. 2 + 2 starting stats.
  5. Choose perks and convert leftover points into stats.
  6. Spend 1 ability point in the T1 branch.

docs.title: Body and Wounds
docs.html:
On the game sheet, each part is shown separately on a drawing of the body. Character health is not given as a number; health is tracked through the limbs. Wounds taken, bandages applied and armor condition are tracked here.

LIMB DAMAGE STATES

Intact → Scratched → Lightly Wounded → Badly Wounded → Unusable → Severed

The phrase "the wound advances 1 stage" means the limb moves to the next state in this order. "The wound drops 1 stage" means it returns to the previous state.

If a bandage gets dirty it loses its effect and the limb becomes Bandaged (Dirty).

There is no augmentation in Umbra Caelis. A severed limb can be replaced with a dwarf-crafted prosthetic, a wooden leg or an iron hook. docs.title: Mana
docs.html:
In Umbra Caelis, mana is an energy given off by all beings. It takes different names and behaves differently depending on the being that emits it. Magic is the act of making these different manas touch one another. This page summarizes the setting's mana system from the player's point of view; the full lore texts are in the Systems/Sorcery folder.

TYPES OF MANA

TypeSourceBehaviorIn play
Inner ManaEvery living thing with a soulProduced very fast, lives very briefly, easy to directThe trigger of magic. Efsun measures it. Shinigami's Flow pool comes from it.
Outer ManaInanimate objects: stone, metal, earthProduced very slowly, lives very long, hard to directThe fuel of great spells. Runes, crystals, Glockenschlag.
Blu ManaInner mana channeled into ores that store outer manaStored; released when brokenCrystals; purification, extra power for spells, noble jewelry.
Decayed ManaMana that has been displaced, shattered or put under extreme pressureUnusable; drains the mana of any soul it touchesThe source of Corruption. The Catastrophe branch turns it into a weapon.
Primordial ManaUnknown; believed to belong to the godsUnknownWhat the Divine branch seeks.

HOW MAGIC WORKS

Inner mana alone isn't enough for more than small tasks; there is little of it and it fades at once. A sorcerer extends their inner mana like a limb and touches outer mana with it. Inner mana is a spark that sets outer mana in motion. Fire magic is a good example: the sorcerer strikes mana grains against each other to make a spark and reach a flame.

No one senses mana from birth. After heavy theoretical training and long meditation, a person senses their own inner mana, then learns to use it to read the presence and amount of the outer mana around them.

Some people don't fit this balance. Someone whose inner mana is weak and short-lived may draw outer mana better than anyone; for them outer mana is not something others prod from afar but an organ of their body. (The Outward Soul perk represents this.)

DYNAMISM

Inner mana has one of three dynamisms depending on how stable the soul is. Dynamism shapes the character's personality and style of magic; mechanically it is expressed through perks and branches.

DynamismHow it flowsIn magicIn play
NormalProduced in the soul, flows outward slowing down, stays just outside the bodyNothing specialDefault.
HighFlows outward very fast until its short life endsEnergy is released as the grains shatter; hard to control, low efficiency, highest explosiveness and regenerationUnleashed and Berserker branches, Volatile Mana perk.
LowAlmost never leaves the bodyAll grains move together in harmony; efficient, calm, low explosiveness; stabilizes the soulShackled branch, Calm Mana perk. Works like medicine for the pains of high dynamism.

GAME RULES

  • Spell roll: Any action roll made with mana; usually d20 + Efsun. Some branches use Hikmet or Sebahat (stated in the ability file).
  • Backlash: On a Nat1 on a spell roll, the mana breaks loose. The character rolls d20 + Sebahat (the GM sets the difficulty, usually Easy); on a failure they gain +1 Corruption. Some abilities and perks change this.
  • Decayed roll: Rolls made with Decayed Mana, dead souls, esoteric faiths and dream powers. Details are on the Corruption page.
  • There is no mana pool. Spells are not spent from a pool; their limits are set by abilities' uses, costs and Corruption. The only exception is the Flow pool of Shinigami, which keeps the release open and fills up each combat.
  • Mana sense: A trained sorcerer senses magic cast nearby, powerful crystals and Decayed Mana zones (Hikmet or Efsun, the GM decides). The Mana Sense ability and the Mana-Sensitive perk make this easier.

DECAYED MANA ZONES

Places left behind by great spells, wars and the Kızıl Kıyamet, where mana has decayed. The meteor is believed to have come from a cursed stone that emits decayed mana. A zone recovers on its own over time, but this can take years.

  • On spell rolls made in the zone, a 1-2 counts as a Nat1.
  • Someone who stays in the zone for a long time (the GM decides, usually one night) rolls Sebahat (Medium); on a failure, +1 Corruption.
  • Because outer mana is corrupted, techniques that draw outer mana (Glockenschlag, Rune Script) do not work in the zone.
  • Breaking a Blu Mana crystal in the zone cleanses the surrounding atmosphere for one scene.

BLU MANA

Some ores do not radiate their static mana but store it inside. When low-dynamism inner mana is channeled into these ores, the two manas merge and form Blu Mana. The resulting ore is called a Blu Mana Crystal. Sorcerers say a drop put into one becomes ten drops; they exaggerate, but not by much.

  • Purification: During a long rest, a crystal is broken and if d20 + Sebahat (Hard) succeeds, Corruption decreases by 1.
  • Power: Breaking a full crystal grants a bonus to the next spell or rune roll (see Crystal Binding).
  • Jewelry and ornaments: Nobles have flasks and jewelry made from Blu Mana for show; sorcerers carry the same jewelry as protection against Decayed Mana.
  • Crystals are expensive and hard to find.

BerserkerTurns high dynamism into rage
ShinigamiInner mana crystallized in steel (Animus); Flow
RunecasterOuter mana, runes, Blu Mana
WizardTriggers outer mana with inner mana

docs.title: Corruption
docs.html:
Abbreviated as Decay on the character sheet. It is a value between 0 and 15. The starting value is 0.

In Umbra Caelis, using magic displaces and shatters mana. Mana that decays turns into Decayed Mana and, like a vacuum, drains any soul it touches to repair itself. Corruption is the void this draining opens in the soul. As the void grows, something seeps in: the voice of dreams. Some call it the God of Dreams, others simply "the voice".

Corruption is not a list of penalties. At every fork your soul makes a decision: surrender to the voice and draw power from it, or resist it and pay the price with your own body. Two characters at the same Corruption level look nothing alike because of the decisions they made.

HOW CORRUPTION INCREASES

  • A Nat1 on a spell roll followed by a failed Sebahat roll (+1).
  • Abilities whose cost is Corruption.
  • Staying a long time in Decayed Mana zones or touching it directly.
  • Using Düşotu (see below).
  • Encounters with the God of Dreams, its creatures and dream horrors (GM).

HOW CORRUPTION DECREASES

Purification with Blu Mana, Prayer and Archpriest abilities and some potions reduce Corruption. Decisions made at forks are not erased. Even if the character drops below a fork, they keep carrying that fork's Surrender or Resistance effect. When they reach the same fork again, they do not make a new choice.

  • Ring floor: Every fork where Surrender was chosen makes the first level of that ring a floor (Fork I → 1, Fork II → 4, Fork III → 7, Fork IV → 10). Corruption cannot drop below this floor. Resistance leaves no floor; a soul that resists the voice can be cleansed.
  • Purification limit: A character's Corruption decreases by at most 2 per session in total from all sources (abilities, Blu Mana, potions).

DECAYED ROLL

Rolls made with Decayed Mana, dead souls, esoteric faiths and dream powers. The ability file carries the note "This ability's rolls are decayed rolls". The table below grants bonuses to decayed rolls (+1 each at Decay 1, 7 and 13, at most +3 in total); some perks and faiths impose penalties. These bonuses also count toward the bonus cap (see Core Rules).

CORRUPTION TABLE

The 15 levels are divided into five rings. The first two levels of each ring are the same for everyone. The third level is a fork: the player chooses the path of Surrender or Resistance, and the decision is permanent. The last ring has no fork; there, the decisions you made are settled.

RING I · STIRRING

DECAY 1: Your dreams gain color and you remember them when you wake. +1 to decayed rolls.
DECAY 2: Your shadow doesn't quite match the light; it lags a moment behind. Someone looking carefully (Görü, Hard) notices something is wrong; -1 to Cazibe rolls against whoever notices.
DECAY 3: Fork I · Whisper. The voice speaks your name for the first time.

  • Surrender · Listening Ear: Once per session you ask the voice a question and it answers. The GM secretly rolls a d6: on 1-4 the answer is true, on 5-6 it is a lie. The GM doesn't say which.
  • Resistance · Closed Door: +2 to Sebahat rolls against mind control, dream and fear effects. Cost: your sleep is broken; -1 to your first roll after each long rest.

RING II · SEEPAGE

DECAY 4: You see Decayed Mana with the naked eye, like a gray shimmer in the air. Holy healing abilities work one step harder on you.
DECAY 5: Animals dislike you. Horses shy, dogs bark; -3 to rolls involving animals.
DECAY 6: Fork II · Hunger. The void inside you wants to be filled.

  • Surrender · Leech: When you hit a sorcerer (or a being that carries magic), you drain its mana: +2 to your next roll, -2 to its next spell roll. Twice per combat.
  • Resistance · Fast: Düşotu and similar substances don't work on you; they neither calm you nor give Corruption. +2 to all rolls you make against Corruption increases.

RING III · CRACK

DECAY 7: Your reflection in the mirror lags a moment behind. On consecrated ground (Sanctuary, Consecrated Ground, churches) -1 to all your rolls. An additional +1 to decayed rolls.
DECAY 8: Lost Moment. At the start of each combat you roll a d20. If the result is Corruption − 5 or lower, the GM plays your first turn, not you; the voice acts in your place.
DECAY 9: Fork III · Name. The voice asks something of you. The GM sets a demand: an item, a secret, someone's blood, the breaking of an oath.

  • Surrender · Covenant: You fulfill the demand. Permanently +1 to your Efsun or Sebahat. The consequences of the demand follow you through the story.
  • Resistance · Refusal: You refuse the demand. A limb of your choice permanently goes cold (Scratched; it never heals by any means). In return the voice leaves you alone for a while: your Corruption does not increase for that session.

RING IV · VOID

DECAY 10: You no longer need to sleep, but if you do, you wake with difficulty. To wake from a long rest you roll Sebahat (Medium); on a failure you wake one scene late. You can see the dream of someone sleeping near you (no roll, only images).
DECAY 11: Your voice is heard in two layers. +2 to Hakimiyet rolls, -2 to Cazibe rolls.
DECAY 12: Fork IV · Door. The door between dream and reality passes through you.

  • Surrender · Dreamwalk: You can enter the dream of someone sleeping (d20 + Efsun (Medium)). In addition, once per session you can undo a wound taken in the last turn by counting it as "a dream".
  • Resistance · Seal: You seal your soul with your own hand. Corruption increases are always applied as at most +1. Cost: your mana is sealed too; -2 to spell rolls.

RING V · FALL

DECAY 13: The voice is now visible. Trifarium believers and priests roll Sebahat (Medium) when they see you; those who fail flee or attack. An additional +1 to decayed rolls.
DECAY 14: Reality thins. The GM may narrate scenes to you differently from the other players and hide some things from you alone.
DECAY 15: The End. Your decisions are settled.

  • 3 or 4 Surrenders · The Unwaking: Your soul passes to the voice. The character becomes the GM's character and returns to the story as a hand of the God of Dreams.
  • 3 or 4 Resistances · Broken Seal: Your soul shatters but remains yours. The character dies; before dying they play one last scene: for 3 turns all their rolls count as successful.
  • 2 Surrenders, 2 Resistances · The In-Between: Your soul belongs neither to you nor to the voice. The player and the GM decide the character's end together.

DÜŞOTU (SOMNARIA)

A purple-leafed plant that grows around Kharadon, dried and burned like incense or drunk as tea. It calms instantly, soothing fear and pain. The more is consumed, the more vivid dreams become. Common folk call it "the breath of the sleeping god". Instead of Düşotu, the GM may also introduce other substances with the same effect (crushed poppy, black wine, Xitochi incense).

A character who uses Düşotu calms down and is freed from negative mental conditions such as Cower, fear and stress. They then make a Corruption roll:

You roll d20 + Sebahat − Corruption/3 (round down) (Medium); on a success Corruption does not increase. On a failure, +1 Corruption.

For characters at Ring IV and above, Düşotu does not give Corruption; the dream is already within them.

PURIFICATION WITH BLU MANA

Blu Mana crystals cleanse the surrounding mana atmosphere when shattered. If a Blu Mana crystal is shattered during a long rest and d20 + Sebahat (Hard) succeeds, Corruption decreases by 1. A crystal is single-use, valuable and hard to find.

classes.name: Close-Quarter
classes.introHtml:
The class of the sword, the axe and the bare fist. Close-Quarter is the path of those who close the distance to their enemy to an arm's length. The knightly orders of Leit'ateirr, the Cataphar heavy cavalry of Blaze, the Düskarls of Ironsmith and nameless mercenaries all know the same truth: in the end, war is the collision of two bodies.

EXAMPLE PATHS

  • Brute → Berserker → Shinigami: A monster that feels no pain, gone mad together with the soul of its sword.
  • Swordsman → Arcanist → Duelist: The flaming swordmaster of the Blaze court.
  • Swordsman → Berserker → Duelist: An honorable but hot-blooded Pad'astra knight.
  • Brute → Arcanist → Shinigami: A warrior who presses mana into their weapon with raw force until, at last, the weapon awakens.

NOTE

Melee attacks are rolled with Yalman (heavy weapons, grappling) or Kaçınç (light weapons, swordplay), depending on the weapon. The GM decides.

classes.name: Hunter
classes.introHtml:
The hunter fights at a place and time of their own choosing. The Drizhina archers of Silverarrow, the Bayezid scouts who vanish into the forests without a trace, the Falltrupp raiders of Von Midon and the monster hunters who sharpen their blades against the horrors of Kharadon are different ends of the same branch.

classes.name: Priest
classes.introHtml:
In Granterra, faith has marched more people than the sword. The Priest class carries faith in two directions: the holy hand that brings the god's power down into the world, and the voice that turns people's will in a single direction. Some priests close wounds, others set crowds ablaze. And some put themselves in the god's place.

The Priest path holds two tendencies. You are free to choose between branches, but their spirit can be summed up like this:

  • Holy Power: Prayer → Will of God → Archpriest. The hand that wields the god's power.
  • Will and Word: Preacher → Men of Will → Occultist. The voice that rallies the party, gives its followers will, and in the end turns them into puppets.

faiths.name: Trifarium (Holy Trinity)
faiths.html: The dominant religion of Es'terra. It calls for the destruction of everything unholy. The priest is devoted to one of three gods:

options.name: Tenebri (Darkness)
options.html: The god of destruction. You grow stronger not while blessing and healing, but while fighting: +1 to Yalman rolls in combat.

options.name: Excidis (Existence)
options.html: The god of life. +1 to healing and resurrection rolls. The Resurrectio roll gets one step easier.

options.name: Aequtris (Justice)
options.html: The god of balance. +1 to Cazibe and Hakimiyet rolls made for interrogation, judgment and persuasion.

faiths.name: Religion of the Mighty Dragons
faiths.html: The religion of the Dragon Dynasty on the western continent. The priest is devoted to a mighty dragon and the emotion it represents (such as anger, honor, sorrow, greed or hope). In scenes where you openly live and show that emotion, you get +2 to one roll (once per scene, with GM approval).
faiths.detailHint: The mighty dragon and emotion you are devoted to (e.g. anger, honor, sorrow, greed, hope)

faiths.name: Vjolfunism
faiths.html: The monotheistic religion of the Burkut Khanate. The priest chooses one of two paths:

options.name: Path of Valor
options.html: +1 to Sebahat rolls as long as you do not retreat in combat.

options.name: Path of Nature
options.html: +1 to healing and Sebahat rolls made in nature.

faiths.name: Tvolktur
faiths.html: The pantheistic, peaceful religion of Aokiba. It holds trade above war. If you did not start the combat, your allies get +1 to their rolls in the first turn of combat. +1 to bargaining and mediation rolls.

faiths.name: Esoteric Faiths
faiths.html:
Cult of Unending Eclipse, Thousand Faces of Trepidation and Order of Starless Knight. These faiths are practiced in secret.

  • You start the game with +1 Corruption.
  • +1 to decayed rolls.
  • If your faith is exposed, you become a wanted person in Trifarium lands (Gesucht-like effects are applied by the GM).
  • Abilities that openly require holy power, such as Manus Dei and Consecrated Ground, work as decayed rolls for esoteric priests and give +1 Corruption on each use.
  • Members of the Order of Starless Knight worship the God of Dreams without knowing it. The GM can send these priests dreams whenever they like.

classes.name: Scholar
classes.introHtml:
Mana is not sensed from birth. It is learned after heavy theoretical training and long meditation. Scholars are the keepers of this knowledge: theorists carving runes in academies, mages who trigger outer mana with their inner mana, and talents wrestling with the dynamism of their own soul. At the far end stand those who reach for the decayed mana that brought the Kızıl Kıyamet, or for the mana of the gods.

MANA SUMMARY

  • Inner Mana: Mana produced by living beings; short-lived and easy to manipulate. Great spells are not cast directly with inner mana; inner mana is used to trigger outer mana.
  • Outer Mana: Slow, long-lived mana emanating from inanimate objects. The source of runes and crystals.
  • Dynamism: Depending on the stability of the soul, inner mana has Normal, High (explosive, uncontrolled) or Low (efficient, calm) dynamism.
  • Decayed Mana: Mana that has undergone decay. It drains the mana of any soul it touches.
  • Primordial Mana: Mana believed to belong to the gods, about which nothing is known.

EXAMPLE PATHS

  • Runecaster → Shackled → Divine: A mage of patience and precision; a soul calm enough to touch the mana of the gods.
  • Wizard → Unleashed → Catastrophe: A disaster ready to repeat the Kızıl Kıyamet on a small scale.
  • Wizard → Shackled → Catastrophe: A dangerous theorist who works decayed mana in cold blood.
  • Runecaster → Unleashed → Divine: A seeker who chains their own explosive soul with runes and tries to look to the heavens.

NOTE

This class's spell rolls are subject to the spell roll rules in the Core Rules: on a Nat1 the mana backlashes: roll d20 + Sebahat, and on a failure gain +1 Corruption.

duelist.name: Duelist
duelist.introHtml: Swordmasters who get lost in the crowd on the battlefield die. The Duelist always reduces the battle to a two-person scene. They read their opponent, wait for the first mistake and never allow a second.

mechanic.title: Duel
mechanic.html:
The Duelist fights not a crowd but a single rival. Reducing combat to a two-person scene is the essence of the branch.

  • Declaration: In combat, without spending your turn, you declare one enemy your Duel Rival. You can have only one rival at a time. If your rival falls, flees or surrenders, you can declare a new rival.
  • Opening: Each time you negate an attack your rival aims at you by dodging or parrying, you gain 1 Opening (maximum 3).
  • Spend 1 Opening to get +2 on one attack against your rival, or to reroll your dodge roll against one of your rival's attacks.
  • Spend 3 Openings on an attack against your rival: if it hits, the wound advances 1 additional stage.
  • Breaking: If you attack someone other than your rival, or an ally attacks your rival, the duel breaks and your Openings are cleared. If your rival leaves you to attack someone else, the duel does not break; your next attack against them gets one step easier.
  • Openings are cleared at the end of combat.

shinigami.name: Shinigami
shinigami.introHtml:
Some weapons outlive their owners. Others fight so long breathing the same mana as their owner's soul that they awaken. These weapons are called Soul-Swords (Animus). Born when inner mana accumulates in steel over years and crystallizes, it is a spirit with its own name, its own personality and its own will.

The Shinigami is the warrior who speaks with their soul-sword, learns its name and finally bends it to their will. The sword is released in two stages: Erwachen (awakening), the first release; Apotheosis (deification), the final release.

mechanic.title: Flow
mechanic.html:
What keeps the release open is the owner's inner mana. Inner mana is produced very quickly and depleted very quickly; this is why the Shinigami enters each combat with a full Flow pool.

  • Flow pool: Efsun + (Sebahat / 2, round down), minimum 2. Refills at the start of each combat.
  • At the end of each turn Erwachen is open, 1 Flow is spent.
  • At the end of each turn Apotheosis is open, 2 Flow are spent.
  • If Flow runs out, the release closes at the end of that turn.
  • Spend 1 Resonance to gain 2 Flow (see Jinzen).

SOUL-SWORD DESIGN

A player who chooses the Shinigami branch designs their own soul-sword together with the GM. The design consists of the sections below and is written on the character sheet:

  1. Name: The soul-sword's true name. The moment the character learns this name through Jinzen or within the story, Erwachen Level 1 unlocks without spending a point; until then, Erwachen cannot be used.
  2. Spirit: The sword's personality and appearance (an old knight, a little girl made of flame, a silent wolf). The GM plays this spirit in Jinzen scenes and in Voice of the Sword moments.
  3. Theme: The essence of the sword's power. An element (flame, ice, lightning), a concept (shadow, sleep, blood, echo) or an emotion.
  4. Release Word: The short phrase that opens Erwachen ("Awaken, ...", "Bleed, ...", "Burn, ...").
  5. Erwachen Form and Effect: According to the budget below.
  6. Apotheosis Name, Form and Effect: According to the budget below. The name of the Apotheosis form is usually given in a sacred language (Latin, German, Spanish).
  7. Weakness: Every soul-sword has a weakness (it is extinguished in water, weakens in moonlight, will not open unless blood is spilled). The weakness is decided between the player and the GM and gives the GM a story hook.
  8. Demand style: What kinds of things the soul-sword will ask of its owner (an honorable fight, blood, silence, loyalty to an oath). Gains meaning with Jinzen L3.

POWER BUDGET

Minor effect (choose one or design something similar):

  • +2 to a specific type of roll (attack, dodge, Görü, Giz).
  • On a hit, a 1-turn condition on the target (burn: 1 stage at the end of the turn; freeze: cannot move; blindness: Görü -3).
  • Reach: The sword can attack at a short distance (about 10 meters).
  • Defense: Once per combat, an incoming wound is reduced by 1 stage.

Major effect (choose one or design something similar):

  • On a hit, the wound advances 1 additional stage.
  • Area: One attack is directed at all nearby enemies, with a separate roll for each.
  • The condition effect lasts 2 turns, or it inflicts Cower (Sebahat Medium).
  • The sword's theme makes a tangible change to the scene (freezing the ground, putting out the light, cutting through a wall).

Apotheosis budget: All of Erwachen's effects are doubled (bonuses and durations) and a final effect is added. The final effect is on the level of the Vertex abilities of T3 branches (a 2-stage blow that hits without a roll, controlling a 10-meter area for 2 turns, immunity to a rule for a scene, and so on).

EXAMPLE SOUL-SWORDS

Rosa Carmesí (Crimson Rose)

  • Spirit: A red-haired woman with a crown of thorns, whose face cannot be seen.
  • Release Word: "Bloom, Rosa Carmesí."
  • Erwachen (L2): The sword splits into rose petals. On a hit, the wound advances 1 additional stage (major).
  • Apotheosis, Jardín de la Sangre: The scene turns into a 10-meter garden of crimson roses. The most exposed limb of every enemy moving in the garden advances 1 stage at the end of each turn; the Erwachen effect becomes 2 stages.
  • Weakness: During Apotheosis, you roll Sebahat (Medium) each turn to tell friend from foe; on a failure, you attack the nearest person.
  • Demand style: Blood. If a combat ends without bloodshed, Rosa sulks.

Aschenkönig (Ash King)

  • Spirit: A half-burned old king sitting on a throne.
  • Release Word: "Turn to ash, Aschenkönig."
  • Erwachen (L1): The sword scatters searing ash. On a hit, the target is blinded for 1 turn (minor).
  • Apotheosis, Asche zu Asche: An ash storm covering the area. Everyone except you gets -6 to Görü rolls; the Erwachen blindness lasts 2 turns; once, a 2-stage blow without a roll against a target in your line of sight.
  • Weakness: Erwachen will not open in rain or underwater.
  • Demand style: Respect. It does not want to open against enemies it considers beneath it.

Somnus (Sleep)

  • Spirit: A child whose eyes are always closed, who talks in their sleep.
  • Release Word: "Sleep, Somnus."
  • Erwachen (L3): The sword becomes invisible; +2 to attacks (minor), inflicts Cower on a hit (major), +2 to dodge (minor).
  • Apotheosis, Somnus Aeternus: The scene turns into a dream. For 2 turns, enemies see the reality you want them to see; one enemy attacks their own ally.
  • Weakness: The God of Dreams recognizes this sword. +1 additional Corruption on each use of Apotheosis.
  • Demand style: Sleep. It steals its owner's long rests; sometimes it wants to dream in their place for a night.

Glacies Vigil (Ice Sentinel)

  • Spirit: A knight in ice-covered armor bearing the old coat of arms of House Frost.
  • Release Word: "Hold your watch, Glacies Vigil."
  • Erwachen (L2): The ground freezes (major). Enemies moving on the frozen ground must make a Kaçınç Medium roll.
  • Apotheosis, Invierno Eterno: For one scene, everyone except you and your allies makes a Yalman Medium roll each turn; those who fail cannot move that turn. Once, you freeze an enemy completely (they cannot take actions for 2 turns).
  • Weakness: In hot regions (Realm of Sand), the Flow pool starts at half.
  • Demand style: Oath. It demands that promises be kept; every broken oath silences it.

perks.name: Dreamweed Addict
perks.html:
You are addicted to Düşotu. Withdrawal: If you go a day without using Düşotu, you roll Sebahat (Hard) after a long rest; on a failure, −1 to all rolls the next day and an additional −2 to Sebahat rolls. The penalty grows by 1 each day until you use Düşotu.

perks.name: Vow of Mercy
perks.html:
You swore never to shed blood. Each time you harm someone else, you gain +1 Corruption. If you kill, you gain +3 Corruption.

NOTE: The GM may not approve this perk for a fighting character. A character in a support role taking this perk calls for scenes where the oath is truly tested.
